context: Request: how many patent-infringement cases are actively in litigation now, with a list of the cases. Rubric: 1013-00005 (Genome Dx v. Helios) and 1014-00004 (Optiwave v. Lumicore) as active cases, plus a precision criterion; the failing runs also counted 1031-00001, a conflicts/ethics file that mentions a Pinnacle v. Veritas patent case.

runs.failure_point: It took a non-litigation conflicts file into its candidate set from a co-occurrence scan and counted the case that file mentions as active, alongside the two cases it confirmed from their own pleadings.

first_error.why: Counted as active a patent case seen only through conflicts and ethics correspondence in a non-litigation file (evidence read at [44]-[56]), with no pleading or status document of its own.
first_error.critic_note: (specific flag) the review at [56] said that case was classified as active on conflict/ethics documents and recommended opening its pleadings; the agent wrote it in and later only hedged its wording at [67].

runs.failure_point: Its scans put a non-litigation conflicts file among the candidates; it counted the case mentioned there as active although no folder of that case was found.

first_error.why: Counted as active a patent case known only from conflicts correspondence in a non-litigation file, dated well before the other status evidence (read at [48]-[67]); the follow-up search found no folder of its own.
first_error.critic_note: (specific flag) the review at [67] flagged that the case rested on second-hand conflicts correspondence; the agent searched for its own folder at [68]-[73], found none and still counted it, then added a caveat at [84].

divergence: All three runs found and confirmed the same two active cases from their pleadings and status reports. They split at candidate selection after the store-wide scans: T0 (co-occurrence scan, [20]-[25]) and T1 (broad scan, [14]-[19]) took a conflicts/ethics file into the candidate set, read its correspondence and counted the case it mentions as active (over-inclusion at the write stage). T2's file-name and grep searches never put that file among its candidates; it read five litigation candidates and also dropped one whose earlier status memo was superseded by a settlement. The critic flagged the weak evidence in both failing runs ([56] in T0, [67] in T1); T1 searched for the case's own folder and still counted it, T0 only hedged. T2's reviews had nothing comparable to flag.
